correctness.rationale: For n>=2 the two-row ladder P2 square Pn admits local column states (a,b) in {0,1,2}^2. For triples (p,s,t), each zero entry of s must have its neighboring row and horizontal weights >=2. Let delta(s)=sum(s)-1 and the finite integer potential d(p,s) as explicitly tabulated in the frozen source. Exhaustive independent enumeration of all 9^3=729 triples found 666 feasible and verified delta(s)+d(p,s)-d(s,t)>=0 in every feasible case; exactly 161 zero-cost triples. Summing telescopes to weight>=n with nonnegative endpoints. The source fully enumerates 13 trimmed zero-cost pair-states and yields two starting row choices, with alternating excursions of uniquely recoverable lengths 1,2,5 and a terminal opposite-column state. The corresponding exact generating function is 2*z^2/(1-z-z^2-z^5), with gamma_I=n and a2..a5=2,2,4,6. Independent exhaustive vertex-label checks for n=2..5 verify minima and counts; the unrestricted all-n statement depends on the complete local certificate/finite transition classification, not on extrapolation.
